upstream.note: Every upstream citation below was read at this revision, the ref docs/PARITY_GAP_ANALYSIS.md pins. github.com/tailscale/tailscale was cloned shallow at tag v1.102.4 and HEAD verified as bbcd7d1fc2054b9189ebc1531acf74bd880ca0c8.

summary.note: This edition replaces the previous one (#459 through #482; those rows remain in git history). It audits the six ports merged after it: #484, #497, #530, #538, #544 and #547. Each was re-read diff by diff against github.com/tailscale/tailscale at v1.102.4. #497 was listed twice for audit (the initial port and its review round), and it has one row covering both, because the squash merged both. All six rows carry at least one divergence from the upstream behaviour their own diff claims to port. There are eleven findings, two major and nine minor, each citing the Go file and the pinned commit it was read at. Many of the minor findings were disclosed in the PR bodies but never ported. They are filed anyway, because a disclosed divergence is still a divergence.

gate.detail: All four steps green on current main (c872cca) plus this report, with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, RUST_TEST_THREADS=4, TS_RS_EXPERIMENT=this_is_unstable_software and toolchain 1.95.0. The four steps were `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-targets` (41 targets, 1243 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored) and `cargo build --release --bins`. tests/parity_audit_ledger.rs passed 6 of 6 against this edition. Two things about the machine, not the tree. First, the default nightly has no clippy, so the gate ran on the installed 1.95.0, the crate's rust-version. Second, the first test run failed only tailnetd's cleanup_refuses_live_socket, with `path must be shorter than SUN_LEN`, because the session's 66-byte TMPDIR overflows darwin's sun_path. Rerun under a short TMPDIR with --no-fail-fast, every target passed.

auditedPrs.notes: Squash 84f399d. Go's sentence is now unbroken on the first line of output, but the refusal still runs ahead of Go's earlier darwin-root fatal and still is not Go's one bare line. The commit also cites upstream at 53a0d659 rather than the ledger pin bbcd7d1 (v1.102.4). The code was re-read at bbcd7d1 and the bird guard there is the same.

Squash 4dce9c2. This one row covers both beads listed against #497 (the initial port and its review round). self_change rides net_map frames, including the initial-netmap front-load, as Go's SelfChange does. But a self-only netmap update sends nothing (engine gap, ENGINE_ASKS #46, disclosed), and the payload is a 5-field subset of tailcfg.Node.

Squash a787db8. set and check-prefs now judge the composed prospective pref, like editPrefsLocked. The route rule now follows the auto-update rule, as in checkPrefsLocked. Three gaps. The new config-file refusal has no Go counterpart: initPrefsFromConfig never runs the check. The up ingress (begin_up) is still unguarded. And the refusal text is not checkAutoUpdatePrefsLocked's sentence.

Squash a38687b. The four CheckTag reasons and the tag: %q frame match tailcfg.go and up.go byte for byte on ASCII input. What tnet up actually prints still differs from Go's stderr. run_up adds an error: prefix, and the check only runs daemon-side. Non-printable bytes are quoted with Rust Debug, not %q.

Squash a8b5fbf. The four named refusals now print bare, as Go's main does. The two --service refusals from the same function still print under anyhow's Caused-by framing (disclosed in the PR). And check_serve_flags_or_exit still runs its refusals in a different order from runServeCombined.

Squash c872cca. Every serving run is now armed, it exits 0 on interrupt, and the pref is restored only on !cgi && started, as runWeb does. The arm still starts after start_tailscaled_web_client's status/prefs/EditPrefs round-trips, where Go arms on runWeb's first line.

findings.title: A netmap update that changes only this node never reaches a watcher as self_change
findings.detail: Upstream builds Notify.SelfChange from NetMap.SelfNode on every netmap update and sends it. That covers a key-expiry extension, a MagicDNS rename or new addresses with no peer delta. Its doc names containerboot, kube agents and sniproxy as consumers who react to exactly that. The merged daemon attaches self_change only to a net_map frame. At engine pin 9d847a6e the engine ticks net_map only when the peer snapshot changes, so a self-only update produces no frame at all until some later peer change. This is disclosed as engine ask #46, and the fix belongs in the engine, but the ported field misses the case it exists for.

findings.title: --config AutoUpdate.Apply=true is refused at boot where Go accepts it
findings.detail: Upstream's config-file ingress never calls checkPrefsLocked. initPrefsFromConfig (at startup) and setConfigLocked (on reload) run conf.Parsed.ToPrefs(), then p.ApplyEdits(&mp), then pm.SetPrefs / setPrefsLocked. So Go starts with "AutoUpdate": {"Apply": true} even where feature.CanAutoUpdate() is false. The merged Config::apply_to_prefs bails with "config: AutoUpdate.Apply: ...". Backend::apply_config propagates that with `?` from tailnetd's --config step, so the daemon refuses to start on a config Go would run. The commit presents this as a port of checkPrefsLocked, but upstream has no such refusal on this path.

findings.title: `up` never checks a stored auto-update opt-in; Go's EditPrefs does
findings.detail: Upstream's `tailscale up` changes prefs through LocalClient.EditPrefs (and Start). editPrefsLocked composes p1 = CurrentPrefs + edits and runs checkPrefsLocked(p1). So an AutoUpdate.Apply=true already persisted on an installation that cannot update fails `up` just as it fails `set`. After this PR, begin_set and check_prefs compose the prospective value through prospective_auto_update, but Backend::begin_up has no auto-update check at all. `tnet up` therefore succeeds on exactly the posture that `tnet set` and `tnet check-prefs` now refuse, although the PR claims the rule holds "on every ingress".

findings.title: Auto-update refusal text is not Go's checkAutoUpdatePrefsLocked message
findings.detail: Upstream's checkAutoUpdatePrefsLocked returns exactly "Auto-updates are not supported on this platform." It returns "Auto-update support is disabled in this build" when HasClientUpdate is off. The merged message is the host reason (a longer sentence, or a Homebrew-specific "not supported on this installation: ..."), then a Hostinfo.AllowsUpdate explanation, then an ingress-specific remedy (REMEDY_CLI / REMEDY_CONFIG). On the config path it also carries a "config: AutoUpdate.Apply: " prefix. Go's sentence survives as a substring on the platform arm only.

findings.title: self_change carries 5 snake_case fields, not Go's tailcfg.Node
findings.detail: Upstream Notify.SelfChange is the whole *tailcfg.Node (json omitzero): StableID, Name, Addresses, KeyExpiry, Tags, CapMap/Capabilities, PrimaryRoutes and the rest. Its doc says consumers read "addresses, name, key expiry, capabilities, etc." from it. The merged SelfReport carries only stable_id, name, ipv4, ipv6 and key_expiry, under different key names. A consumer ported from Go that reacts to a tag or capability change on its own node gets nothing. This was a disclosed decision, but it narrows the ported field.

findings.title: `tnet up` prints the tag refusal behind `error: `, and only from the daemon
findings.detail: Upstream prefsFromUpArgs rejects the tag in the CLI, before any LocalAPI call. Go's main prints the returned error bare, so stderr is exactly `tag: "foo:bar": tags must start with 'tag:'` and it is printed whether or not tailscaled is running. In the merged code the check lives only in the daemon (complete_and_validate_advertise_tags). run_up renders the daemon's Response::Error as `eprintln!("error: {message}")`, so a human-mode `tnet up --advertise-tags foo:bar` prints `error: tag: "foo:bar": ...`. With --json it prints a {Error} object instead. With no daemon running it reports a connection failure instead of the tag refusal. The commit's claim that tnet now prints Go's line holds only for the string inside the message.

findings.title: Tag quoting uses Rust {:?}, not Go %q, for non-printable bytes
findings.detail: Upstream formats the refused tag with %q (strconv.Quote rules, e.g. a 0x01 byte is written \x01). The merged frame uses Rust's Debug ({t:?}), which writes the same byte as \u{1}. The output is identical for printable ASCII, the case the tests pin, but diverges for control characters. Those are exactly the bytes CheckTag's last clause refuses.

findings.title: The two --service refusals in runServeCombined still aren't Go's bare line
findings.detail:
Upstream returns errors.New("Error: --service flag is not supported with funnel") and errors.New("Error: --service flag is only compatible with background mode"), and main prints them with a bare Fprintln: one line each. After this PR the merged tnet still prints `Error: funnel via <socket>

Caused by:
    --service flag is not supported with funnel` (and the serve/background twin), as tests/serve_refusal_stderr_framing.rs records. The PR fixed the rendering for four refusals in the same function and disclosed these two as still divergent. They remain unported.

findings.title: Serve refusals are checked in a different order from runServeCombined
findings.detail: Upstream runServeCombined checks in this order: verifyFunnelEnabled (funnel only), then cleanURLPath, then srvTypeAndPortFromFlags, then the two PROXY checks, then GetServeConfig, getLocalClientStatusWithoutPeers, the HTTPS enable flow and 'service hosts must be tagged nodes'. Only after all of those does it check 'tun mode is only supported for services'. The merged check_serve_flags_or_exit runs all four now-bare refusals as a pure pre-flight, before any LocalAPI call. So with the daemon down, Go reports 'error getting serve config: ...' for `serve --tun 3000` while tnet prints 'tun mode is only supported for services'. For funnel, Go's funnel-capability refusal comes before the mount-point and PROXY refusals.

findings.title: `tnet web` arms SIGINT after its startup round-trips; Go arms first
findings.detail: Upstream runWeb's first statement is signal.NotifyContext(ctx, os.Interrupt), so an interrupt during StatusWithoutPeers, GetPrefs or setRunWebClient(true) is caught. The cancelled ctx fails the in-flight call ('starting web client in tailscaled: context canceled', exit 1), or, once the pref is set, the goroutine turns it back off and exits 0. The merged run_web calls start_tailscaled_web_client (Status, GetPrefs, then EditPrefs) before web_interrupt() is first polled. A Ctrl-C in that window still dies on the default disposition with status 130, and can leave RunWebClient on. The commit says the arm now precedes the pref step as Go's does, but it doesn't.

findings.title: --bird-socket refusal still isn't Go's one bare line, and fires too early
findings.detail: Upstream sets log.SetFlags(0) and calls log.Fatalf("--bird-socket is not supported on %s", runtime.GOOS). Its whole stderr is one line with no prefix and no full stop. Go reaches that check only after the darwin 'tailscaled requires root' fatal and the '--socket is required' fatal. The merged binary prints `error: --bird-socket is not supported on this platform or in this build of tailnetd.` and then several explanatory paragraphs. It also runs this refusal before its own darwin root refusal (tunflag::darwin_root_refusal), so a non-root macOS run with both conditions gets the BIRD message where Go gives the root one. The PR defends the `error: ` prefix because "every fatal refusal on this binary" has one. But the neighbouring darwin root refusal is printed bare to match Go, so that rationale does not hold.
